_comment: SD17 -- the Burrow Warrens, the Meadows' one required dungeon (MEADOWS_PROGRESSION_SPEC.md Sec3 Band 2). A COMPACT cave, not a puzzle box: five chambers, one gated side branch, aggressive Ground creatures, Rootstone in the walls, and one guardian that has to be beaten. ALL NUMBERS TUNABLE per CLAUDE.md. scripts/world/burrow_warrens.gd is the only reader.
_comment_site: `entrance.at` is world metres [x, z]; `entrance.yaw_deg` turns the cave's LOCAL +z (its depth axis) toward the rocky rise at [140,-90], so walking in walks INTO the hill. The site was measured, not guessed (a throwaway probe over data/config/terrain_playground.json's own heightfield): [70,-140] is the flattest approach of five candidates on that flank -- 8 degrees of local relief over 4m against 46-54 degrees at every candidate further up the flank, which the spawns.json header already records as unwalkable ground. Terrain along the depth axis climbs 0.3 -> 10.7 -> 20.9 -> 27.0m at 0/20/30/40m in, so the mouth chamber's roof breaks the surface as a rocky outcrop and everything past it is genuinely buried. It sits ~143m south-east of the village square, past where the deeper Meadows begins, and a short walk from the Burrowback cluster spawns.json already places at [55,-145] -- the warrens is where they come from.
_comment_floor: The cave floor is ONE level, `floor_clearance` above the terrain height at the mouth. What makes a flat floor honest here is no longer rising ground -- see `_comment_resiting`: there is no rising ground in this part of the Meadows, and the cave stands in a rock knoll of its own on the flattest ground within 60m. A flat floor is what that site supports; a descending one would put the ground surface inside the deeper rooms. `wall_thickness`, `skirt` (how far floor slabs and walls extend BELOW the floor, so nothing floats where the hillside falls away) and `rock` colours are presentation, all tunable.
_comment_ow5d_relocation: OW5D, docs/specs/MEADOWS_MACRO_LAYOUT.md section 10.2: `site.at` moves from (70,-140) to (-420,2470). Everything else in this file (chambers, passages, lights, spawns, deposits, prize) is authored in the SITE'S OWN LOCAL frame per `_comment_site`/`_comment_floor` above and rotates/translates with `site.at`+`site.yaw_deg` automatically, so none of it needed editing. `yaw_deg` (54.5) is left UNCHANGED -- the relocation table gives only a new position, not a new approach bearing, and re-deriving it for the new site's actual hillside would need fresh ground probing (this file's own `_comment_site` explains the original 54.5 was picked from a 5-candidate probe of the OLD flank at [140,-90], which no longer describes anything at the new site). Ground truth at the new site was NOT probed by this pass (see the OW5D report) -- flagging per the macro-layout doc's own instruction that `burrow_warrens.json`'s 10m `skirt` needs ground that will accept it. `harvest.json`'s five ironwood nodes move with this site at the same offset (-490,+2610).
_comment_resiting: BAND2-63-WARRENS, 2026-08-22. `site.at` moves to (-357,2610) and `yaw_deg` to 315.0, from OW5D's (-420,2470)/54.5. The reason is not taste: at the OW5D site the cave could not be walked through. `tools/_probe_warrens_run.gd` drove the player in and wedged them solid at local z=27.5 against a collider named `Terrain`, five metres short of the passage to the den -- the guardian, the clear flag and the heartstone were all unreachable on foot, and `tests/smoke_warrens.gd` never saw it because it teleported the player into each chamber rather than walking between them. The cause is the one OW5D's own `_comment_ow5d_relocation` (below, kept) wrote down and left open: it translated a cave whose geometry had been measured against a specific steep flank at (70,-140) onto ground nobody had probed, and kept the bearing derived for the old flank. At (-420,2470) the ground rolls; it does not rise. `tools/_probe_warrens_site.gd` measures that chamber by chamber, and its modes rule out the obvious fixes in turn: another bearing does not clear it (`--scan`), no origin on a 25m grid out to 300m clears it (`--sites`, run from this site AND from the Old Quarry -- the best anywhere is 2.6m short of burying 4-6m ceilings), and making the cave DESCEND (`--plan`) buries the deep rooms but not the entrance, because the ground surface then cuts through the entry corridor and the player walks up it into the ceiling. There is no flank in this part of the Meadows. What works is `--mound`: stand the cave where the terrain never rises above its floor at all, so nothing intrudes anywhere, and let what shows above ground be a rock knoll with a hole in it -- which is what this file's own site comment always said the entrance was, and what `skirt` was built to hide the underside of (see `_comment_mound` for the outcrop that makes it read as stone rather than as a slab). The first such site, (-382,2510), cleared the footprint and failed the OTHER half nobody had checked: the driven run walked 30m from the road and stopped 25m short of the entrance, against a 50-degree bank. `--best` scores both at once -- footprint clear, the 40m in front of the mouth walkable, and the site kept near the spine -- and (-357,2610) at 315 degrees is its answer: clear by 0.43m, approach 6.9 degrees, 34m off the spine, sitting on the `warren_undertrail` loop that terrain_playground.json already runs past the warrens. The whole path now walks: road to entrance to mouth to hall to den to vault, 123m, 26s, measured. Everything sited against the old mouth moved with it: Pell's stand (trainers.json order 2001, 35m out on the approach), the five ironwood nodes (harvest.json), the warrens' own resident Burrowback cluster (spawns.json order 3) and the map region (map_landmarks.json). The chamber layout, sizes, spawns, deposits, dressing and prize are UNCHANGED -- they are authored in the site's own local frame and rotate with it, which is the property `_comment_site` describes. One dependency is NOT this lane's to close: the scatter still has a `CommonTree_3` standing in the new doorway, because a band clearing does not invalidate the bake (GATE_D_LANE_CONTRACT.md sec4). The clearing is authored (bands/band2_stone_and_root/vegetation.json order 2002, radius 30) and the walked evidence above was measured with the 93 scatter colliders inside it dropped, which is what the coordinator's single re-bake will do for real.

bank._why_restart: OP-0905-09 CLEAN RESTART, 2026-09-06. Owner: "Burrow warrens looks awful from the outside", no qualifier, after ten dressing rounds (EXT-04..EXT-10 above, kept in this file's own history) retuned a boulder GRID that never stopped reading as a rock pile with a small dark metal-framed doorway in a field. This key REPLACES the old `mound` block outright: `burrow_warrens.gd`'s `_build_bank()` now builds ONE procedural earth-bank mesh instead of a scatter of Rock_Medium placements. Every field below is read only by that section of burrow_warrens.gd -- see its own header comment for the shape math.
bank._why_shape: The bank is a smooth union of one cone per chamber (mouth/hall/warren/den/vault), each sized so that chamber's own centre clears its ceiling by `clearance_m` plus `safety_m`. `margin_m` is the radius past each chamber's own outer wall the cone falls to zero over -- it is also what sets the natural flank/back slope (peak/radius), so 7m against this site's own chamber sizes lands in the 20-30 degree band the brief asks for without a separate slope knob. `blend_k` softens the seam where two cones overlap (bigger = smoother, and always OVERSHOOTS rather than undershoots the true max, so it can only ever help the clearance guarantee).
bank._why_crest_boost: SECOND-PASS-0906, judge evidence 'smaller than the tree beside it ... no landmark silhouette here at all'. The chamber cones above size the dome purely for CLEARANCE (each chamber's own ceiling + `clearance_m` + `safety_m`), which at this site's own ceiling heights (3.4-4.8m) never asked for a mound taller than ~7-8m -- correct for enclosure, short of a landmark. `crest_boost_m` is ADDED to every chamber's own `p` in `_bank_chamber_bumps()`, so it can only ever give MORE clearance than the guarantee needs, never less; the brief's own '>=10.5m, >=5.8x the 1.8m trainer' bar is what 3.5m of boost clears against this site's own tallest chamber (den).
bank._why_crest_boost_round4: ROUND-4-0906, JUDGE-round3.md 'a single smooth ridge': `crest_boost_m` lifts EVERY chamber's plateau uniformly, which is exactly what drew a 55m-wide flat ridge at 10-12m with one crown -- measured on the height field (tests/smoke_warrens_fixture.gd now prints the skyline's local maxima). 3.5 -> 1.5 drops the plateau so the crown and the new `mounds` below stand proud of it; the crest itself is kept at ~15m by `crown_amplitude_m` 8 -> 10.5. The enclosure guarantee (top + clearance + safety) is untouched by either.
bank._why_crown: SECOND-PASS-0906, judge evidence 'a single flat brown slab with a hard, straight top edge'. Diagnosed directly (a throwaway height-field probe, not assumed): past the notch's own width, `_bank_union_height()`'s `mouth` cone barely reaches in Z (its taper is centred on the CHAMBER's own far centre, not the doorway), so the union height a metre or two either side of the arch is already ~0 -- and `_bank_apply_face_carve()`'s `min(h, plane)` can only ever LOWER a tall `h` to match a shorter `plane`, never raise a near-zero `h` to meet a taller one, so the shoulders beside the arch were reading as bare ground plus noise with no intentional shape at all (the actual 'flat, textureless' slab). `_bank_crown_bump()` is a second, ADDITIVE-ONLY dome centred `crown_offset_z_m` behind the doorway (into the hill, the 'rounded dome behind' the brief asks for), added in TWO places: inside `_bank_apply_face_carve()`'s own `top_at_line` (so the cliff's anchor line itself is not flat) AND, separately, added directly in `_bank_height_at()` AFTER the carve (scaled by the same `(1-settled)` the noise bump uses, so it fills in the shoulders' own missing mass without ever re-admitting height into the open doorway corridor a player walks through). `crown_radius_x_m` is wide enough that the shoulders keep sloping continuously out past `face_half_width_m` instead of dropping to flat zero a metre off the arch; `crown_radius_z_m` a little wider still so the bump reads as one continuous mass with the mound rising behind it, not a second, separate hump.
bank._why_mounds: ROUND-4-0906, JUDGE-round3.md finding 1 ('no landmark silhouette: one smooth ridge'). Secondary dig-mounds / spoil heaps, read by burrow_warrens.gd::_bank_mounds_from_config() -- see _bank_mound_term()'s own header for the shape (asymmetric dome, elongated along `yaw_deg`, longer `throw_radius_m` on the throw side than `back_radius_m` on the hole side, `across_radius_m` sideways, `bare_throw` how strongly its throw lobe reads as raw spoil). ADDITIVE ONLY on top of the chamber cones; folded in BEFORE the face carve so a heap at the face is cut to the same plane. Positions are LOCAL (x, z), z0 = 1 is the dome-face doorway, -z is the way out. The two brow heaps flank the mouth (their throw lobes point out and down toward the threshold, the direction a digger throws), the warren and vault heaps sit over those chambers' own bulges where their warren holes are, the back heap closes the far side. TUNABLE: the fixture asserts >=3 skyline maxima with >=1m prominence.

With the bank's own surface now carrying strata, mossy ledges and crevice shadow (`geology` below), the scattered Rock_Medium props are no longer needed to say 'rock' and were the thing actually reading as plastic: `face_outcrops` 7 -> 3, `accent_boulders` 8 -> 4, `skirt_count` 70 -> 44. bank._comment_geology: WARRENS-ART-0906 round 5. OWNER 2026-09-06: 'the placed rocks on the exterior don't look right. it seems like you can do something more like what we're doing on cloudreach cliffs with the cliffs to make this look better rather than using plastic prop assets.' Both blind rounds had already found it from the pictures alone -- round 1 'flat hard-edged facet slabs with a painted-on moss band ... needs rock forms with real strata', round 2 'the boulders are flat-shaded low-poly slabs with hard facets and visible triangle edges, while the knoll they sit on is a smooth high-resolution blob with a noise texture. Two incompatible rock treatments, adjacent, in the same shot.' The answer is not more props. This bank is already a procedural surface with a shader on it, so the rock goes IN the surface: where the mound is steep enough to be a cut face rather than a settled slope it draws stone with sedimentary banding, mossy ledges and crevice shadow -- the same three moves `shaders/cloudreach_cliff.gdshader` makes, sharing that shader's own Rock030 texture. The PALETTE is deliberately Cloudreach's option A, the grey-green granite the owner picked on 2026-09-06, so the two biomes' stone is one material language instead of tan-vs-grey. Every key maps 1:1 onto a `rock_*` uniform via `_apply_geology()`; `strength` 0 or no block at all reverts the whole layer.

geology._why_round5b: First attempt overshot, measured on this lane's own render: at strength 0.85 with a 44-60 degree band, the whole DOME qualified -- this mound's settled flanks already sit near 50 degrees (the fixture measures the dug face at 45-48) -- and Cloudreach's cliff palette is tuned for a shadowed vertical cliff, not a sunlit meadow bank. The knoll came back as a near-black cone (01-knoll, 03-mouth). Two corrections, both about WHERE and HOW DARK rather than about the technique: the band moves to 52-68 degrees so only genuinely cut, near-vertical faces take stone and the grassy dome stays grass, and the palette lifts a full step with the crevice darkening roughly halved, because a bank in full meadow sun is not a cliff face in its own shadow. _comment_interior_rock: CONTENT-0828. The owner localised the looks complaint on 2026-08-28 -- 'burrow warrens and the castle are the lame looking locations. basically everywhere we had to build an under ground or build a building' -- and this is the half of the answer that needs no owner art. The terrain, scatter and grass drew no complaint; the two ASSEMBLED spaces did, and this cave's own before-frames say why: archive/reports/docs-evidence-full/content-0828/04-vault-prize-after.png is a perfect rectangular box -- four flat walls meeting at hard 90-degree corners, a flat ceiling, a flat floor, one triplanar texture at one scale over all of it, next door to a meadow with hundreds of pieces of variety per comparable area. It does not read as unfinished because the rock texture is bad. It reads as unfinished because a cave does not have corners. So this breaks the three junctions that say 'box' and nothing else: the wall/floor line (boulders banked along the inside of each wall), the wall/ceiling line (rock in the four ceiling corners only -- the ceiling's MIDDLE stays clear on purpose, because rock over the guardian's head is the frame this pass exists to stop producing) and the flat floor (scree thinning inward from the walls). Everything sits within `edge_band_m` of a wall, so the middle of every room is untouched and a den fight keeps the arena combat_arena_bounds_at() promises it; nothing goes in a doorway; and none of it has colliders, the rule _build_site_skirt()'s own comment states -- this is dressing, and a pebble that stops a player is a bug. Same nature family as the outcrop outside and the same `mound.tint`, per D24: the stone inside the hill and the stone showing above it are the same stone. `enabled: false` turns the whole pass off. ALL TUNABLE.

interior_rock._comment_tint: Round 1 of this pass reused `mound.tint` (#c3bbab) and the frames said no: that value was tuned against the outcrop standing in DIRECT SUN, and under the cave's dim cool pools the nature pack's mint-grey came back through it -- the same green a blind critic called 'a heap of enormous cabbages' on the mound in BAND2-63 round 1, now inside the room. `_tint_rock()` multiplies albedo, so the tint has to do the whole job of turning mint into stone here rather than assisting sunlight. This is pulled hard toward the cave's own `site.rock` warmth: against the mint source it lands a warm brown-grey, which is the colour the walls three feet away already are. Interior and exterior rock are still the same models from the same family (D24); they are lit by different light and so they are tinted for it.
interior_rock._comment_material: Round 2 tinted these rocks twice and the frames said green both times. `_tint_rock()` MULTIPLIES albedo, which is the right tool outside -- it keeps each rock's own shading under strong sun and two blind rounds tuned the mound with it -- but under 0.3-1.5 energy pools the multiply does almost none of the work and what survives is the model's own mint texture. So the interior rock now wears the SAME triplanar Rock030 material the chamber walls wear (burrow_warrens.gd::_wear_the_cave_stone). Triplanar is what makes that legal on models whose UVs were authored for something else -- it projects from world space and needs no UVs, the same reason the walls use it on primitive boxes. `tint` is no longer a colour correction; it is the per-piece VARIATION, each rock taking the site's own rock colour nudged 35% toward this value so a bank along a wall is not one flat sheet of identical stone.
interior_rock._comment_caps: Round 2 capped HEIGHT and said nothing about WIDTH, and the frames showed the cost: a five-metre-wide rock sitting correctly against the den wall still reaches two and a half metres into the room, and one ended up between the camera and the guardian -- the exact failure this pass exists to replace. Both caps are metres, applied to each piece's MEASURED bounds rather than to a scale factor, because these models arrive at different sizes and a scale number means nothing across them.

_comment_interior_structure: CONTENT-0828B. The other half of the owner's 4a diagnosis, and the half `interior_rock` above deliberately did not attempt -- its own report: 'the walls themselves are still flat planes and the ceiling is still a slab between its corners. This pass changes what the room's EDGES do; it does not give the space vertical interest, level changes, or a silhouette.' The owner named a CLASS of space ('basically everywhere we had to build an under ground or build a building'), so the answer is a shared method rather than a second dressing pass on one cave: scripts/world/interior_structure.gd, which stronghold.json consumes from the same file with its own vocabulary. That file's header carries the mechanism; the short version is that a chamber built from six flat boxes has exactly two scales of incident (the room, and its props) where the meadow outside has five or six, and that missing MIDDLE scale is what makes an interior read as blockout however good its texture is. The five passes put it back: a vertical member at a repeating pitch along every wall (`bays`), a jointed horizontal band at mid-height (`course`), ceiling ribs landed on the same divisions so the structure reads as continuous (`ribs`), a jamb-and-lintel frame around every cut opening (`reveals`), and a post in each internal corner (`corners`). None of it is solid, none of it enters a doorway, and none of it reaches further into a room than interior_structure.gd's own MAX_PROJECT_M -- half the metre `combat_arena_bounds_at()` reserves from every wall, so the den fight keeps the arena it was tuned against. ALL TUNABLE; `enabled: false` turns the whole pass off.
_comment_interior_structure_cave: This cave's VOCABULARY, against the castle's. `jitter` above zero is the whole difference in code: each member takes a small lean, inset and scale variation, so the same rhythm that reads as masonry in the stronghold reads as rock ribbing here. 0.85 rather than 1.0 because past that the members stop lining up with each other and the rhythm -- which is the point of the pass -- stops reading. `bay_pitch_m` is tighter than the stronghold's (2.9 against 3.6): these chambers are 7-16m across and 3.4-4.8m tall, and a pitch tuned for a 28m hall gives a small room one member and no rhythm at all. `tints` are per-role value steps off `site.rock`; they exist because every light in this cave is a shadowless omni (`_build_lights`), so nothing here is going to model the form for us and a member the same value as the wall behind it is invisible however well it is shaped. Omit a role and burrow_warrens.gd::_structure_colour derives it.

interior_structure._comment_ragged: CONTENT-0828B round 4. `jitter` alone did not make this read as a cave: a blind critic given the ribbed build said nothing in the Warrens reads as burrowed and that it is 'built out of the same dressed ashlar as the fortress'. Fair -- a few degrees of lean on a member that still runs floor to ceiling at a regular pitch is a colonnade with a wobble. `ragged` gives each member its own height and width, so ribs DIE OUT partway up the wall the way harder stone in a cave does, and a member that stops short loses its capital because a capital is a thing masonry has and rock does not. `ragged_short_at` is the shortest a member may be as a fraction of the wall. Set `ragged: false` for masonry.
interior_structure._comment_corbel: A bracket under each end of every ceiling rib. The same critic's first finding was that the ribs 'simply penetrate the masonry -- nothing sags, nothing is broken, nothing carries a load'. A corbel is what a wall does to catch a beam; it also puts a second silhouette on the wall/ceiling line, which is the junction this whole pass is about. 0 removes them.

_comment_guardian_combat_profile: WALL (G-3's table) plus G-9's own two additions. WALL is `enemy` defaults (power 8, telegraph 0.55, recovery 0.75, chase_speed 4.6, reposition_distance 4.0) with `telegraph 0.85`, `recovery 1.1`, `power x1.5` (8 x 1.5 = 12), `chase_speed 3.4`, `reposition_distance 2.5` -- slow, heavy, stands its ground, a long and expensive punish window. G-9 adds `lunge 6.5` and `cone_degrees 72` so the swing the player actually sees matches Earth Fist's own authored arc (`_comment_guardian_move` above: '0.62s windup and a 72-degree cone... directional, so a player who reads the windup can step around it') rather than the generic enemy's 90-degree cone and 3.4 lunge. Every key not named here falls back to `combat.json`'s `enemy` block untouched, per G-2's own merge rule. WHAT THE FIGHT IS SUPPOSED TO FEEL LIKE, for the coordinator to check their merge against: the guardian should read as slow and grounded rather than fast -- it does not chase eagerly (chase_speed 3.4 against the field's 4.6) and it does not circle back in quickly after a swing (reposition_distance 2.5, tighter than the field's 4.0, so it plants and waits rather than repositioning far). Its telegraph should be VISIBLY longer than a den resident's before this pass (0.85s against the residents' unmodified 0.55s, a 0.30s gap -- G-9's own floor, met exactly rather than padded past it) so a player who has learned to read the field's 0.55s tell gets a beat more warning here, not less. The hit itself should read as heavy and worth stepping out of -- power 12 against the field's 8 is a full one-and-a-half step up, meeting G-9's own 1.4x-over-a-den-resident floor with margin -- but the WALL profile's long 1.1s recovery is deliberately the throw window G-10 requires: a player who steps around the swing gets a real, generous opening to either land a hit or throw an orb, so the guardian reads as dangerous to fight carelessly and never reads as unfairly fast or as a wall nothing can get through. `lunge 6.5` (up from the field's 3.4) means that when it does commit, the reach is real -- in the den's own ~6m of clearance (this file's `_comment_chambers_heights`), that is most of the room, so 'stepping around it' is a real spatial decision inside a tight chamber, not merely dodging a jab. TUNABLE, but changing these numbers changes what G-9's own fails-if bar is checked against -- re-derive with `combat_math.base_damage` before retuning power.

Two causes. SCALE: the three species carried multipliers picked per-species by eye, and the Oyster mesh is a multi-cap cluster, so four instances put twelve caps in a 3 m passage. Every `scale_mul` is now derived from the model's own native height so all three land near 0.46 m at a cluster scale of 1.0. VALUE: `emission` roughly halved and every `albedo` tint dropped about a quarter -- these are glowing fungus in a dark cave, and they have to sit UNDER the lit floor in value or they stop being a light source and become the subject. The 2026-09-04 round-2 note below made the same correction in the same direction and is kept as the record of it.
fungus._comment_round2: Round 2: at emission 1.5 the pale caps blew out to white blobs (after1 frame 03). Emission 0.55 on a darkened albedo: green glow, not a white flare.
